On Thu, Mar 17, 2022 at 12:09 PM Rezha Bayu Oktavian Arief [contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi LF and USAID teams,
Apologies for our late response.
Overall the Program Description looks good to us. There are some questions and ideas from USAID team
that we believe LF team can help respond and address. However, just to share some thoughts around
some of these ideas:
• We believe it makes sense to eventually mix up the university selection based on area with low and
high digital literacy index based on Kominfo's latest survey, so there's a cross learning among the
students from different location and so they can share best practices on the FB group as we
envision these students to be part of a group/community
• It also makes sense to consider adopting Merdeka Belajar (Min. of Education) into this program, but
potentially in the next phase in the coming years, by convincing the participating universities to
include this program in the curriculum outside of their study program and so students can get credit
as well. Or another alternative that we can think of is to include this program as part of the
university's community service program scheme, so students can use this opportunity to also
engage and outreach other people and to get credit for their study as well.
These are just some additional thoughts from us to think of, but once again overall the doc looks
good to us.
Thank you, LF and USAID team for the thorough and collaborative work on this!
ciand

On Fri, Feb 25, 2022 at 1:11 PM Matt Love < [contact omitted]> wrote:
Dear Walter, Qisa'i and USAID colleagues,
We now have confirmation from Facebook on the preferred contract term and funding level for the
Indonesia University challenge. The preference is for a 2 year contract. Under this arrangement, USAID
and FB will each contribute $250k per year (cash and in-kind). Breakdown as follows:
Year 1 (June 2022-May 2023)*
USAID: $250k cash contribution
FB: $70k cash + $180k in-kind
Year 2 (June 2023-May 2024)*
USAID: $250k cash contribution
FB: $100k cash +$150k in-kind(exact split TBD)
*Exact contract dates to be discussed and confirmed with USAID.
Please let us know if this sounds agreeable to you. If so, Love Frankie will update the program description
(the live Google doc) to reflect this timeline and level of investment.
Thank you all.
Matt

Matt Love

On Fri, Feb 4, 2022 at 12:10 PM Hwee En Tan < [opaque block] [contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi everyone,
Starting a new thread with everyone from the USAID, FB and LF teams.
Thank you for all your time yesterday, it was great having everyone in the same room!
Here's sharing notes and next steps from our conversation.
In terms of the next time we all get together again for the program description working
session, please let us know your availability for w/c 14 February and we'll coordinate a
call timing.
USAID: How will we measure the success of this program? How will we know that
we have changed behaviours?
• M&E impact tracking through two aspects:
• Impact of how capacity building for the university participants (primary
audience) by doing a pre-and post-survey
• Qualitative research on the impact of the primary audience's knowledge on
the topic
Follow-up_question from USAID:
• How do you tell that the content is being looked at? Engaged with? How are they
engaging with it? How are they responding?
• Are there other things that can be done to showcase the impact of the other
groups beyond just the primary audience?
USAID: Why did we decide to focus on communications students?
• Base capacity to create content that will resonate with other students

• Also selecting micro influencers who have the reach and capacity to reach other
students
• The comms students that we've engaged with previously also included students
specializing in journalism, marketing, etc
• Open to explore if we should open up the student criteria to other faculties as well
Follow-up_question from USAID:
• How have you identified those students in the past?
• Are there criteria we will put in place to ensure secondary reach?
USAID: Would you consider a multi year partnership? More universities engaged?
The universities that USAID already has economic programming?
USAID is interested in doing a longer-term project (3-4 years) - more interested in the
long term impact and results. Would like to build in check points over 12 month periods to
adjust and iterate. Program idea works really well with Internews, Notre Dame, Moonshot,
etc.
Facebook's budget cycle runs year to year - i.e., difficult to sign off budget for multi-year
projects upfront, but keen to explore longer-term partnership as well.
We're all open to working with USAID's existing university partners if we collectively
decide that they are the right fit.
Follow-up_question from USAID:
• Facebook to sense check if we are able to explore this as a longer-term
engagement
USAID: Challenges & learnings from past projects
• Adapting to COVID restrictions - having to pivot from online, key challenge in
sustaining students' engagement digitally throughout the length of the project by
keeping the program inspirational and aspirational. Good opportunity to evaluate
upfront what our engagement approach is (online vs offline vs hybrid).
• Capturing holistic impact across audience tiers - how can we create knock-on
effects to secondary audiences, and so forth?
• Moderating students' work - putting in place clear guidance and boundaries while
maximizing space for creativity
•Importance of building cohesive relationships with teachers and student contacts
for seamless communication and planning
USAID: Is there any possibility of mitigating the kind of risk where the skills
learned turn into something more violent or corrupt?
• To explore risk mitigation plan further
FB: Sharing of USAID program materials and background information
We have consolidated the materials shared during the call here.
Feel free to add in any other resources or links in the document directly!
Next steps:
: FB and LF to huddle internally on the follow-up questions above
FB, LF, USAID to proceed to the co-creation phase for program description based
on concept note
• GDA evaluation typically takes 4-16 weeks
Feel free to add on to any of the points above.
Thanks all, have a restful weekend!
Regards,
Hwee
-

Ahmad Qisai, Ph.D
Anti-Corruption Advisor
Office of Democratic Resilience and Governance
USAID/Indonesia
